protocol.name: treeland_output_group_manager_unstable_v1
protocol.copyright: SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2024 - 2026 UnionTech Software Technology Co., Ltd. SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
protocol.description:
This protocol lets a privileged client such as the DDE display settings panel organize physical outputs into mirroring groups: one source output whose rendered content is duplicated to one or more mirror outputs, so that several screens show the same desktop. This is the "copy mode" of the compositor, as opposed to the default "extension" mode where each output shows an independent desktop region.
The protocol exposes a singleton manager global that creates and tracks treeland_output_group_v1 objects. Each group designates a single source output and an ordered list of mirror outputs, all addressed by opaque uuid strings. While copy mode is engaged the compositor exposes a wl_output global only for the source output; mirror outputs have no wl_output, so their uuids must be obtained from the treeland-output-uuid-head-unstable-v1 protocol rather than treeland-output-uuid-unstable-v1 (see treeland_output_group_v1 for details). An output may belong to at most one group at a time. A group drives copy mode while it has both a source and at least one mirror; a group with no source or no mirrors is inert, the affected outputs get their wl_output back, and they behave as normal extension outputs. An empty uuid represents the absence of a source; output uuids are never empty.
The compositor persists the set of groups and their configuration (name, configured source uuid, and configured mirror uuid list) across compositor restarts and restores them on startup, so groups survive reboots and reappear as group_added events on bind; this lets a privileged client configure mirroring once and have it reapply automatically later. The name never changes; the configured source and mirror list persist until a client changes them with set_source, add_output, remove_output, or dissolve.
The terms "must", "must not", "should", and "may" in this document are to be interpreted as described in RFC 2119.
Warning! This protocol is EXPERIMENTAL and under active development. It may change at any time, including in backward-incompatible ways, without incrementing the interface major version and without prior notice. No compatibility guarantees of any kind are provided. Clients and compositors must track the upstream definition in treeland-protocols and must not rely on the current interface names, requests, events, or semantics remaining stable across releases.

interface.name: treeland_output_group_manager_v1
interface.description:
A singleton global that creates treeland_output_group_v1 objects and broadcasts the set of existing groups to bound clients.
On bind the compositor emits one group_added event per existing group, followed by a single groups_done event, so the client can distinguish the initial dump of pre-existing groups from later group_added events for groups created after the bind. When any client creates a group every other bound client receives group_added for it, and when a group is dissolved every bound client receives group_removed. Clients therefore never poll for the group set; they may also obtain a group object for a known name at any time with the get_group request.
Multiple privileged clients such as the DDE display settings panel may bind and use the protocol concurrently. Requests from all clients are applied in arrival order; an output claimed by one group is rejected for another with the non-fatal output_in_use failure, so concurrent edits never terminate a connection and clients may retry or adjust.

enum.name: error
enum.description: Raised as fatal protocol errors on the manager object.

entry.name: invalid_source
entry.summary: the non-empty source uuid does not identify a connected enabled output

entry.name: invalid_name
entry.summary: the name is empty, or no group with that name currently exists

request.name: destroy
request.description:
Destroy the treeland_output_group_manager_v1 object and release the client's binding to the manager global.
Existing treeland_output_group_v1 objects are not affected and remain valid until they are destroyed or the compositor dissolves the group. The client must destroy each group object separately; the compositor does not cascade destruction from the manager.

request.name: create_group

description.summary: create a new output mirror group

request.description:
Create a new treeland_output_group_v1 object with the given initial source output. An empty source creates a group with no source; the client adds mirrors afterwards with add_output and may change the source with set_source. Copy mode engages once the group has both a source and at least one mirror.
The compositor assigns a unique name to the new group; names are chosen by the compositor, not by clients. The client learns the name from the name event, which the compositor emits on the new group object before any other event. The name identifies the group in the manager's group_removed event. A non-empty source that does not identify a connected enabled output is rejected with the invalid_source fatal error. This check is deterministic, so the compositor raises it on the manager object and does not create the group.
On success the compositor broadcasts a group_added event carrying a new group object to every other bound client; the caller receives its group object only as the new_id return value and does not get a group_added event for it.

arg.name: source
arg.summary: uuid of the initial source output, or empty for no source

request.name: get_group

description.summary: get a group object by name

request.description:
Create a new treeland_output_group_v1 object bound to the existing group with the given name, for example a group created by another client or one whose object the client has since destroyed. On success the compositor sends the initial state of the group on the new object: one name event, then one source event, followed by one outputs event carrying the full mirror list in list order.
The name is the compositor-assigned name reported by the name event on group objects. An empty name, or a name that does not identify an existing group at the time the request is processed, is rejected with the invalid_name fatal error and no object is created; note that a group may have been dissolved between the group_removed event and this request. This lookup is deterministic, so the compositor raises the error on the manager object.
The returned object is an independent handle: destroying it does not dissolve the group, and several clients may hold objects bound to the same group at the same time.

arg.name: id
arg.summary: a new group object bound to the named group

arg.name: name
arg.summary: the compositor-assigned name of the group

event.name: group_added
event.description:
Emitted when a mirror group is created by any client. Each bound client receives this event once per existing group on bind, and again whenever a new group is created — except for the client that created the group, which receives the group object as the new_id return value of create_group instead.
The id argument is a fresh group object; the compositor sends the initial name, source, and outputs state of the group on it immediately after this event. The client may destroy the object if it does not need to observe that group; doing so does not dissolve the group.

arg.name: id
arg.summary: a group object bound to the new group

event.name: groups_done
event.description: Emitted exactly once, after the compositor has finished sending the bind-time group_added events for all groups that existed when the client bound. A client receiving this event knows it has seen the complete initial set and that any later group_added is for a group created after the bind.

event.name: group_removed
event.description: Emitted when a mirror group is dissolved, whether because a client sent the dissolve request or because the compositor removed it as a whole. Every bound client receives this event for the group; any group objects that client holds for it receive a removed event and must be destroyed afterwards.

arg.name: name
arg.summary: the name of the dissolved group

interface.name: treeland_output_group_v1
interface.description:
Represents one mirroring group: a source output, identified by its uuid, whose content is duplicated to an ordered list of mirror outputs, each identified by its uuid. Output uuids are never empty; an empty uuid in events represents the absence of a source.
While the group has both a source and at least one mirror, the compositor exposes a wl_output global only for the source output. Mirror outputs have no wl_output while copy mode is engaged, so clients cannot use wl_output-based protocols (including treeland-output-uuid-unstable-v1, which requires a wl_output) to identify them; they must instead obtain mirror uuids from the treeland-output-uuid-head-unstable-v1 protocol, which resolves a zwlr_output_head_v1 to the same uuid. When copy mode exits — the last mirror is removed, the source is cleared, or the group is dissolved — the affected outputs become normal extension outputs again and their wl_output globals come back.
The group keeps a configured source (zero or one) and a configured mirror list (zero or more), set by the client with set_source, add_output, and remove_output. The source and outputs events report the effective runtime state, not the configured state: a configured source or mirror whose output is currently unplugged or disabled is absent from those events but remains in the persisted configuration, so copy mode auto-resumes when the output comes back. An output may belong to at most one group at a time; one already in another group fails with the output_in_use failure. Copy mode is engaged while the group has both an effective source and at least one effective mirror; otherwise the group is inert and the affected outputs behave as normal extension outputs.
Requests that cannot be applied because of transient output state (e.g. an output unplugged between get_uuid and the request) are reported via a non-fatal operation_failed event; the group is unchanged and the client may retry. Only already_dissolved — sending any request other than destroy on a dissolved group — is a fatal protocol error.
On creation the compositor sends the current state: one name event carrying the compositor-assigned group name, then one source event (empty uuid if no source), followed by one outputs event carrying the full mirror list. Later changes are reported by further source and outputs events; the name never changes.
Several group objects may be bound to the same group, for example one from create_group, one from get_group, and others from group_added; they all observe the same state. Destroying one object only releases that client's handle. The dissolve request tears down the group as a whole, emitting removed to every bound group object and group_removed on the manager. After removed the object is inert: only destroy is valid, and anything else is rejected with the already_dissolved error.
When a member output is unplugged or disabled the compositor updates the effective runtime state without dissolving the group and without changing the persisted configuration: an unavailable mirror is dropped from the outputs event, and if the source becomes unavailable its source event is emitted with an empty uuid — unavailable outputs cannot serve as source, so the compositor does not auto-promote a mirror. When the output comes back (replugged or re-enabled) the compositor re-evaluates and resumes automatically: the source event regains its configured uuid and the outputs event regains the mirror, without any client action. If all of a group's outputs are unavailable the source event is empty and the outputs count is zero, but the group remains and is restored once any output returns. Client-driven remove_output, by contrast, removes the output from the persisted configuration.

enum.name: error
enum.description: Raised as fatal protocol errors on the group object.

entry.name: already_dissolved
entry.summary: the group has been dissolved; only destroy may be sent

enum.name: failure
enum.description: Returned by the operation_failed event when a set_source, add_output, or remove_output request cannot be applied. These reflect transient or dynamic output state (e.g. an output unplugged between get_uuid and the request), not a protocol violation; the client may retry or adjust and the connection is not terminated.

entry.name: invalid_output
entry.summary: no enabled output with the provided uuid is currently connected

entry.name: duplicate_output
entry.summary: the output is already the source or a mirror of this group

entry.name: output_in_use
entry.summary: the output is the source or a mirror of another mirror group

entry.name: not_in_group
entry.summary: the output is not a member of this group

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroy this group object and release the client's handle. The group itself is not affected: copy mode continues, other handles remain valid, and the compositor does not emit group_removed. Use dissolve to tear down the group as a whole. It is safe to destroy an object that has already received the removed event.

request.name: set_source
request.description:
Set the output identified by the given uuid as the source of the group, replacing any current source, which is removed and becomes a normal extension output again.
If the request cannot be applied, the compositor emits an operation_failed event and the group is unchanged: invalid_output if the uuid does not identify a connected enabled output, duplicate_output if the output is already in this group (to promote a current mirror to the source, remove it first with remove_output), or output_in_use if the output belongs to another group.
If the group already has mirrors, this engages or updates copy mode immediately. The compositor confirms the new source by emitting a source event.

arg.name: uuid
arg.summary: uuid of the output to designate as the source

request.name: add_output
request.description:
Append the output identified by the given uuid to the end of the group's mirror list.
If the request cannot be applied, the compositor emits an operation_failed event and the group is unchanged: invalid_output if the uuid does not identify a connected enabled output, duplicate_output if the output is already in this group, or output_in_use if it belongs to another group.
If the group already has a source, this engages or extends copy mode immediately, confirmed by an outputs event carrying the updated mirror list. Sources and mirrors may be set in any order; copy mode engages once both are present.

arg.name: uuid
arg.summary: uuid of the output to add as a mirror

request.name: remove_output
request.description:
Remove the output identified by the given uuid from the group. If the output is not a current member, the compositor emits an operation_failed event with not_in_group and the group is unchanged.
If the output is a mirror, an outputs event carrying the updated effective mirror list is emitted; if the group then has an effective source but no effective mirrors, copy mode exits while the source remains set.
If the output is the source, the configured source is cleared and a source event with an empty uuid is emitted; the mirrors are unchanged and copy mode exits. This does not auto-select a successor; to promote a mirror, call set_source on it.

arg.name: uuid
arg.summary: uuid of the member output to remove

request.name: dissolve

description.summary: dissolve the group and exit copy mode

request.description: Tear down the group: exit copy mode, remove it from the manager, and release the affected outputs. The configured source and mirror list are discarded and the group is not restored on compositor restart. The compositor emits removed to every group object bound to this group and group_removed on the manager. After removed the object is inert; only destroy is valid, and anything else — including dissolve again — is rejected with already_dissolved.

event.name: name

description.summary: the compositor-assigned name of the group

event.description: Reports the name the compositor assigned to this group. Emitted exactly once on each group object, before any other event, so the creator of the group learns its name without a group_added event. The name is unique among existing groups and never changes; it identifies the group in the manager's group_removed event and is the name accepted by the manager's get_group request.

arg.name: name
arg.summary: the compositor-assigned name of the group

event.name: source

description.summary: current effective source output of the group

event.description: Reports the uuid of the current effective source output: the configured source if its output is currently connected and enabled, or an empty uuid when the configured source is unavailable (unplugged or disabled) or when no source is configured. Emitted once on creation and again whenever the effective source changes, including when an unavailable source comes back or an available one goes away; the configured source is restored automatically on return.

arg.name: uuid
arg.summary: uuid of the current effective source output, or empty when none is available

event.name: outputs

description.summary: the full mirror output list of the group

event.description:
Reports the complete ordered list of effective mirror outputs of the group: the configured mirrors whose outputs are currently connected and enabled. Emitted once on creation with the current effective mirror list, and again whenever that list changes: after a successful add_output or remove_output of a mirror, when a mirror is unplugged, disabled, re-enabled, or replugged, or when a mirror is promoted to the source. Each emission carries the full effective list, replacing any previously known list, so the client replaces its state instead of applying deltas.
The uuids argument contains the concatenation of count uuids, one per mirror, in list order. All output uuids have the same length, so each uuid is the array size in bytes divided by count, and parsing needs no separators: the client reads count fixed-length uuids back to back. The count argument always matches the number of uuids in the array; a client may use it to validate the array size. The list order follows the order in which mirrors were added; unavailable mirrors are filtered out without shifting the relative order of the others, and a mirror promoted to the source simply leaves the list. The source output, if any, is not part of the list and is reported separately by the source event; a count of zero means the group currently has no effective mirrors.

arg.name: count
arg.summary: number of mirror outputs in the list

arg.name: uuids
arg.summary: concatenation of count same-length mirror output uuids, in list order

event.name: removed
event.description: Emitted to every group object bound to the group when the group is dissolved. After this event the object is inert and the client must destroy it.

event.name: operation_failed

description.summary: a set_source, add_output, or remove_output request failed

event.description: Emitted when a set_source, add_output, or remove_output request cannot be applied because of a transient or dynamic output state, such as an output being unplugged between get_uuid and the request. The code identifies the failure cause; the uuid is the output the client passed to the failing request. The group state is unchanged and the client may retry or adjust. This is not a protocol error and the connection is not terminated.

arg.name: uuid
arg.summary: the uuid the client passed to the failing request
